I am interested in the intersection of research, public service, and policymaking.
My academic and professional experiences have allowed me to explore issues ranging from Irish social housing policy to congressional reform and impact evaluation.
Through this website, I hope to share some of the projects, research, and experiences that have shaped my work.

title: Projects
text:
Selected Projects
Welcome to my portfolio of research, policy analysis, and data visualization projects.
My work explores questions surrounding public policy, political institutions, and social change through both quantitative and qualitative research methods.





POLICY RESEARCH{.project-category}

Irish Social Housing Policy
An examination of housing affordability, institutional barriers, and social housing provision in Ireland.
Drawing on my experience working in the Irish Parliament, this research explores the structural challenges affecting housing accessibility and considers alternative approaches to social housing provision.
Research Areas: Housing Policy, Public Administration, Comparative Policy
View Irish Housing Project





DATA VISUALIZATION{.project-category}

U.S. Population Trends
An exploration of county-level population and demographic changes in the United States.
Using R and ggplot2, this project visualizes population trends and demographic characteristics to better understand changes across communities.
Tools: R, ggplot2, Data Visualization
View Population Trends Project

Undergraduate Thesis: Political and Social Thought
An independent undergraduate research project completed through the Political and Social Thought program at the University of Virginia.
This project reflects my interest in political theory, social questions, and interdisciplinary scholarship.
Research Areas: Political Theory, Social Thought, Interdisciplinary Research

title: Irish Social Housing Policy
text:
Project Overview
This research examines the challenges affecting social housing provision in Ireland, with particular attention to housing affordability, institutional constraints, and alternative models of housing development.
The project builds upon my legislative internship with TD Mark Wall in the Irish Parliament during summer 2026.

title: Irish Social Housing Policy
text:
Policy Problem
Many low- and moderate-income households in Ireland face significant challenges accessing affordable and suitable housing.
The issue extends beyond housing supply, encompassing development costs, institutional limitations, and barriers to accessing social housing.

title: Irish Social Housing Policy
text:
Research Methods
My research incorporates several approaches, including:

Policy and legislative analysis
Interviews with housing policy experts
Review of academic literature
Comparative analysis of housing models
Examination of institutional barriers

title: Irish Social Housing Policy
text:
Key Areas of Research

Local Authority Capacity
Examining the role of local authorities in the financing, development, and management of social housing.


Housing Affordability
Investigating the relationship between housing costs, household incomes, and eligibility for housing supports.


Alternative Housing Models
Exploring international approaches to affordable housing provision, including cost-rental housing and Vienna’s social housing model.

title: Irish Social Housing Policy
text:
Research Progress
This project is ongoing.
Additional findings, analysis, and recommendations will be added as the research develops.
